description: Hi! I'm William from Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. I'm passionate about technology, science, space exploration, and using creative ideas to solve real-world problems. I enjoy exploring new concepts and collaborating with people from different backgrounds. I'm looking for curious, motivated teammates with interests in programming, research, science, data analysis, or design. Most importantly, I value creativity, open-mindedness, and teamwork. Let's build something meaningful together!
summary:
ARES-NAV is an orbital-to-surface Martian Extravehicular Activity (EVA) navigation system, 3D holographic terrain table, bi-directional CapCom co-op suite, and stereoscopic 3D spacesuit visor built on 219 real NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance and Curiosity mission files.
Mars has no GPS satellites or global magnetic field, turning steep crater scarps, dust-storm whiteouts, and solar proton storms into life-or-death hazards. ARES-NAV solves this across four integrated modes: (1) orbital radiometric PNT tracking via MRO, Odyssey, and MAVEN; (2) an 8-connected A* surface router over real MRO HiRISE and MOLA Digital Elevation Models using 0.38g Pandolf-Santee suit metabolic physics, UHF line-of-sight ray-casting, and Dual-Crew Buddy-Rule O2 reserve checks—saving 24% primary PLSS oxygen; (3) a smartphone-powered stereoscopic 3D AR spacesuit visor synced over Wi-Fi to Mission Control with 20 Hz head-tracking, two-way target marking, and DEM wireframe Synthetic Vision for zero-visibility dust storms; and (4) a SHERLOC Deep-UV and PIXL micro-lab for NASA CoLD biosignature triage and Flight Data File debriefing. ARES-NAV protects astronaut lives while accelerating human exploration and astrobiology on Mars.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

ARES-NAV is an end-to-end Martian Extravehicular Activity (EVA) tactical navigation, telemetry, and astrobiology suite operating across two real NASA landing sectors (Jezero Crater — Site 093 and Gale Crater — Boxwork):

  1. Mode 1 — 360° Orbital PNT Globe: Tracks NASA relay orbiters (MRO, Mars Odyssey, and MAVEN) in WebGL, computing live Horizontal Dilution of Precision (HDOP) via Electra UHF radiometric Doppler/ranging before descending to the surface.
  2. Mode 2 — Surface GPS Map & WebGL 3D Holographic Terrain Table: Runs an 8-connected A pathfinder* over real 100×68 MRO HiRISE (DTEEC_048900_1745) and MOLA Digital Elevation Models. It fuses 0.38g Pandolf-Santee spacesuit metabolic physics, >15° / >25° slope limits, THEMIS thermal inertia sand-sinkage penalties, 401 MHz UHF line-of-sight ray-casting to the Perseverance rover mast, and NASA Dual-Crew (EV-1 + EV-2) 26m Buddy-Rule constraints. Mission Control can extrude 13,266 triangles of real Jezero topography in 3D and fly chase cameras along the route.
  3. Mode 3 — Stereoscopic 3D Spacesuit Visor & Bi-Directional CapCom Link: Scanning an ISO-18004 QR code pairs a smartphone inside a DIY stereoscopic 3D visor with the laptop Mission Control station over local Wi-Fi (<20 ms latency, zero internet required). Astronaut head orientation and hands-free Gaze-Dwell 1064nm SuperCam LIBS laser shots stream to Mission Control at 20 Hz, while Mission Control clicks rocks on the 2D/3D map to project 3D Cyan AR Priority Target Diamonds and Quindar tones directly into the astronaut's goggles. During τ = 3.2 dust whiteouts, Synthetic Vision renders 3D HiRISE DEM ridge wireframes and holographic ground chevrons through zero visibility.
  4. Mode 4 — SHERLOC Deep-UV Micro-Lab & Printable NASA FDF Debrief: Simulates Perseverance's 248.6nm Deep-UV Raman (SHERLOC) and PIXL X-Ray instruments on real Cheyava Falls micro-imagery, resolving vivianite/greigite "leopard spots" and the 1595 cm⁻¹ organic carbon G-band (CoLD Level 4), then exports a complete NASA Flight Data File (FDF) debrief.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Saves Life-Support Consumables: Cuts primary PLSS oxygen consumption by ~24% compared to direct point-to-point climbs while maintaining continuous UHF comms.
  • Survives Worst-Case Contingencies: Enforces NASA's 15% PLSS O₂ Reserve Redline under a +48% metabolic Buddy-Tow Fault and automates a 2-stage emergency abort into natural basalt overhang shelter (-74% radiation dose) during Solar Particle Events or suit leaks.
  • Accelerates Planetary Science & STEM Outreach: Bridges Earth-bound Mission Control and surface crews for future NASA Moon-to-Mars human missions while letting students and judges step onto Mars today using any smartphone and low-cost 3D goggles.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Languages & Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, Vanilla ES6+ JavaScript, WebGL / 3D Canvas, <model-viewer> (NASA .glb 3D meshes of Perseverance, Ingenuity, xEMU spacesuit, and Jezero Crater), Web Audio API (NASA Quindar tones & Perseverance Mars microphone audio), and Web Speech API (hands-free voice commands & suit voice callouts).
  • Backend & Data Pipeline: Python 3 (ares_capcom_server.py zero-dependency multi-threaded HTTP 206 Byte-Range + Server-Sent Events telemetry relay; Pillow asset pipeline compressing 219 authentic NASA PDS Mars 2020 & Curiosity images into WebP).
  • Hardware: Laptop Mission Control station + iPhone/smartphone gyroscope paired via LAN/Hotspot inside a DIY Stereoscopic 3D Magnifying Spacesuit Visor.
  • NASA Data Sources: Mars 2020 Perseverance PDS bundles (Mastcam-Z, Navcam, Hazcam, SuperCam RMI, SHERLOC WATSON/ACI, MEDA SkyCam), M2020 traverse/waypoints GeoJSON, MSL Curiosity PIA26696 Boxwork panoramas, MRO HiRISE DEMs, MOLA global topography, and Mars orbital relay parameters.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • True Two-Way Human-in-the-Loop Co-Op: Rather than building a static map viewer, we turned an everyday smartphone into a live stereoscopic AR spacesuit visor linked bi-directionally to a JPL OnSight-inspired Mission Control console—working 100% offline or over a local phone hotspot with zero cloud dependencies.
  • Authentic Martian Physics & Operational Realism: Our team accounted for Mars's 3.711 m/s² (0.38g) gravity, pressurized 4.3 PSI suit mobility costs, diurnal LTST thermal heater draw, Mie-scattering dust storm optical depth (τ), orbital relay pass windows, hands-free pressurized-glove ergonomics (voice + gaze-dwell), and NASA's 7-level Confidence of Life Detection (CoLD) framework.
